parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing entry, document, facility or criminal trans-specific restriction is documented, and EU free movement applies. Against that, the combined regime shows documented societal and official hostility: a lethal 2022 shooting at an LGBT bar, a commissioner finding LGBTI rights more at risk six months later, a serving minister's 2024 hostile statement, and repeated failed bills to ban legal gender change or transition. Anti-discrimination law covers gender identity in services, but hate-crime law explicitly covers sexual orientation more than gender identity and no working trans-visitor remedy is documented. Healthcare was refused in 2022 after standards were revoked; 2023 republication is unimplemented on the record. Rate consequences if outed, not resident LGR gaps.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry or documentation obstacle documented; regional free-movement rules apply.
entry_documents.protection: Free movement and a 2018 regional court residency ruling with announced compliance.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; resident medicalised LGR and registry refusals are not documented reaching visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No visitor detention, fines, custody placement or police targeting for presentation is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No documented pathway from document mismatch to detention for a visitor.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward or other facility exclusion for visitors is stated.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers gender identity in goods and services generally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No subnational variation documented; national regime is the operative regime.

care_services.exposure: In 2022, after standards of care were revoked, providers were refusing transgender care and people sought treatment abroad.
care_services.protection: Standards were republished 3 March 2023, but implementation in care access is unresolved.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing continuity of care faces uncertain access; no visitor-specific refusal is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Repeated bills sought to ban legal gender change, and a 2023 version would have jailed transition for at least four years; all failed. A karyotype-only bill passed first reading.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No enacted trans-specific criminalisation is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Failed and unresolved bills signal hostile institutional climate but are not operative traveller law.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No rule on a trans minor visitor, accompanied minor, or guardian is stated.
minors_guardians.interaction: No recognition of same-sex relationships is documented for a travelling couple, but no traveller penalty is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A lethal 2022 attack on a capital LGBT bar killed two; the 2010 first Pride was stoned and dispersed. Official and wider public hostility is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers gender identity in services; hate-crime enhancement explicitly covers sexual orientation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Single venue attack must not dominate, but commissioner concern, minister hostility and hostile climate make street exposure real.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented working remedy for a trans visitor facing violence or discrimination; hate-crime law omits gender identity explicitly.
remedies_unknowns.protection: 2004 Anti-Discrimination Act covers gender identity across employment, education, housing, social care and services.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper protection without documented operation for visitors limits mitigation; 2023 care-standards implementation is unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-B: no documented police stops, confiscations, fines or coerced interviews of visitors, and no routine detention for identity checks.
Higher than 0.55-B: no documented secondary screening, refused admission or discretionary border denial for document mismatch; the main risks are societal hostility and uncertain care.

Lower than 0.75-C: protections there include trained border handling and a tribunal that works, whereas here hostile official framing, a lethal venue attack and no documented effective trans remedy persist.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines an open traveller door with a hostile social and political setting. No documented universal exposure or criminalisation pushes the rating down to severe-risk levels, and resident LGR inadequacies are not counted as visitor exposure. But documented hostility, lethal anti-LGBT violence, a two-year-old then-worsening commissioner finding, trans-specific recourse gaps, and uncertain post-2022 care access mean an outed visitor cannot rely on demonstrated protection. That places the case in reduced-risk territory, materially below well-protected anchors yet above routine state screening or exclusion regimes.
